work.title: Plato, Crito
work.notes: Plato's dramatic representation of Socrates in prison. Keep Plato's authorship explicit and distinguish the argument against retaliation from broader, contested interpretations of obedience to law.

edition.label: Benjamin Jowett translation in Standard Ebooks' Dialogues, 2022
edition.licenseNote: The EPUB states that the source text and artwork are believed public domain in the USA and that Standard Ebooks' contributions are dedicated worldwide under CC0 1.0. Verify source-text rights in the deployment jurisdiction.

passages.citationLabel: Plato, Crito 49b–d, Jowett trans., Standard Ebooks
passages.translationText: Socrates Then we must do no wrong? Crito Certainly not. Socrates Nor, when injured, injure in return, as the many imagine; for we must injure no one at all?
passages.interpretiveNote: Jowett's version confirms the core anti-retaliation argument. The dialogue's reasoning should be tested through questions and distinctions rather than reduced to passive acceptance of abuse.
passages.period: Platonic representation of Socrates; historical English translation in a modern public-domain edition
